meta.note: Generic unguided aerial gravity bomb, representative of WW2-era 'dumb bombs'.
Generic loitering munition ('kamikaze drone'), representative of modern systems like the Switchblade.

Real weapon: AeroVironment Switchblade, a backpack-portable 'kamikaze drone' first used in Afghanistan; its small warhead is optimized against personnel and light vehicles rather than armor, hence the much lower blast radius than the dataset's generic DRONE_STRIKE.

Real weapon: ZALA Lancet, a Russian loitering munition that became prominent in the Russo-Ukrainian War for picking off artillery pieces and armored vehicles, hence a higher metal-vs-flesh damage split than the anti-personnel-oriented Switchblade.

meta.realGun: Bayraktar TB2, medium-altitude long-endurance (MALE) armed reconnaissance drone
meta.note: Real weapon: unlike a loitering munition, the TB2 is reusable — it carries and releases small laser-guided smart munitions (MAM-L/MAM-C) and returns to base, and proved highly influential in conflicts in Nagorno-Karabakh, Libya, and Ukraine.

Real weapon: a low-cost, mass-producible loitering munition with a distinctive moped-like engine buzz, launched in swarms rather than individually — its low unit cost rather than precision is its main tactical advantage, reflected here as lower accuracy than purpose-built precision loitering munitions.

meta.realGun: FIM-92 Stinger, man-portable infrared-guided surface-to-air missile (MANPADS)
meta.note: Real weapon: became famous when the CIA supplied Stinger missiles to Afghan Mujahideen in the 1980s, where they neutralized the previously dominant Soviet helicopter gunships — the metal-vs-flesh split here reflects its role as an anti-aircraft, not anti-personnel, weapon.

Real weapon: MG 151/20, a 20mm autocannon fitted to German fighters like the Bf 109 and Fw 190 — heavier hitting than a rifle-caliber machine gun, giving fighters a real chance of downing bombers in single passes.
Real weapon: the Hispano 20mm cannon, which replaced rifle-caliber Browning machine guns on late-war Spitfires and Hurricanes once reliability issues with early mountings were solved.

Real weapon: M61 Vulcan, a 6-barrel rotary 20mm cannon that has been the standard internal gun on US fighter jets since the Vietnam era — a direct technological descendant of the 19th-century Gatling gun already in this dataset.

Real weapon: AIM-9 Sidewinder, first fired in combat during the 1958 Taiwan Strait Crisis — an infrared-guided air-to-air missile whose basic 'heat-seeking' concept remains the ancestor of most short-range air-to-air missiles still in service.

Real weapon: JDAM (Joint Direct Attack Munition), a GPS guidance-and-fins kit bolted onto an otherwise unguided 'dumb' bomb — a cheap way to turn the generic BOMB already in this dataset into a precision-guided weapon, reflected here as a large jump in accuracy for similar destructive power.
Real weapon: AGM-114 Hellfire, a laser/radar-guided anti-armor missile originally designed for attack helicopters and later adapted as the primary strike weapon on armed drones like the MQ-9 Reaper.
